title: Verdier biduality for Weil complexes
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X$ put $\bar X=X\times_{k_0}k$ and let $g_{\bar X}$ be geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. On the small pro-etale site of $\bar X$, let $R_{\bar X}$ be the coefficient sheaf whose sections on a quasi-compact object $V$ are continuous functions $|V|\to\Omega$ with values in one finite intermediate extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$; on general objects impose this condition locally [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]. Write $\mathcal A_{\bar X}=\operatorname{Mod}(R_{\bar X})$ for its module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $\mathcal B_{\bar X}$ for pairs $(F,\theta:g_{\bar X}^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}F)$ in $\mathcal A_{\bar X}$, with intertwining morphisms [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. Derived categories mean localization of complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathrm{WC}(X)\subset D(\mathcal B_{\bar X})$ be the full subcategory with bounded cohomology whose underlying cohomology sheaves admit a finite locally closed stratification with pro-etale locally finite free restrictions over $R_{\bar X}$. This is the native category `AlgebraicGeometry.WeilComplex`, not the category of fixed pairs in $D(\mathcal A_{\bar X})$.

Let $a_0:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ be the structure morphism and let $Ra_{0!}^{\mathrm W}:\mathrm{WC}(X)\to\mathrm{WC}(\operatorname{Spec}k_0)$ be the native compact-support functor `AlgebraicGeometry.WeilComplex.derivedLowerShriek`, formed from equivariant open extension by zero and proper direct image along a compactification [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Assume that $Ra_{0!}^{\mathrm W}$ has a right adjoint $Ra_0^{!,\mathrm W}$ on $\mathrm{WC}$, as in `WeilComplex.HasUpperShriek`. Put $\omega_X=Ra_0^{!,\mathrm W}\Omega^{\mathrm W}$, where $\Omega^{\mathrm W}$ is $R_s[0]$ with its canonical Frobenius pullback isomorphism at $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. For $K,L\in D(\mathcal B_{\bar X})$ let $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal B_{\bar X}}(K,L)$ be the native derived internal Hom `ProEtaleWeilSheaf.derivedHom`: choose a K-injective resolution $L\to I$ in complexes over $\mathcal B_{\bar X}$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex] and take the product total complex $\prod_p\mathcal Hom_{R_{\bar X}}(K^p,I^{p+n})$ of internal Hom sheaves of $R_{\bar X}$-modules, each with the contragredient Weil structure $\theta_I\circ(-)\circ\theta_K^{-1}$ (through the canonical isomorphism $g^*\mathcal Hom(A,B)\cong\mathcal Hom(g^*A,g^*B)$ for the automorphism $g=g_{\bar X}$). Then:

1. for every $K\in\mathrm{WC}(X)$ the object $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal B_{\bar X}}(K,\omega_X)$ lies in $\mathrm{WC}(X)$, so that
$$D_X=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal B_{\bar X}}(-,\omega_X):\mathrm{WC}(X)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{WC}(X)$$
is a functor (Lean `WeilComplex.verdierDual`, the lift through `objectProperty_derivedHom_dualizingComplex`);
2. the identity functor of $\mathrm{WC}(X)$ is naturally isomorphic to $D_X\circ D_X^{\mathrm{op}}$: there is a natural isomorphism $K\xrightarrow{\sim}D_XD_XK$. Clause 2 is precisely `AlgebraicGeometry.WeilComplex.nonempty_iso_verdierDual_rightOp_comp_verdierDual`. The category [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] supplies the blueprint's Frobenius-pair model; it is not used as a definition of this native derived category.

proof.text: Choose the finite-field datum for k0 and its algebraic closure. Obtain the normalized realization family, native exceptional-forgetting package and native section-closed comparison. Supply the actual upperShriek and its actual adjunction as the right-adjoint part of the native comparison datum. The already proved preservation theorem and the nativeModel isomorphism show that its internal Hom into the native dualizing object restricts to WeilComplex.

Apply the existing bidual-evaluation realization theorem to that datum and closure proof. It gives a natural native delta and the exact equation j_K followed by U(delta_K) followed by b_K equals rho(commonBidual(M_K)). Apply the structural common-stage evaluation-invertibility lemma to M_K. The right side is invertible, and j_K and b_K are isomorphisms, hence U(delta_K) is invertible.

Forgetting on the native derived category reflects isomorphisms by native_closed_forgetful. Closure transport is direct image along an isomorphism and its right derivation is an equivalence; the exact section-module presentation is an equivalence as well. Their composite U therefore reflects isomorphisms. Thus every delta_K is invertible and asIso delta is a natural isomorphism. Cancel the fully faithful inclusion on the nativeModel isomorphism to identify the restricted closed Hom with the source verdierDual; whisker this comparison and its opposite to identify their double-dual functors. Compose with asIso delta.
